fields.question: Why not rank candidates by adaptive-subset means?
fields.answer: Rounds differ in coverage and difficulty and favor historical failures. They expose actionable errors, not unbiased full-set performance; selection needs common cases/queries, coverage and regressions.
fields.example: Teaching example: A scores 0.6 on three difficult cases and B 0.9 on three easy ones; this does not establish B is stronger.

fields.question: How do later perfect observations reduce an old failure's influence?
fields.answer: The unresolved-error term divides log(1+error age) by one plus subsequent perfect observations. EMA loss, staleness, count and uniform exploration still jointly determine probability.
fields.example: Teaching example: at the same error age, two perfect observations reduce log(4) to log(4)/3 without deleting the case.

fields.question: Do HoMe and MORSE search the same memory-harness space?
fields.answer: No. HoMe centers on file-memory session differences and evaluation reuse. MORSE adds online research and host-approved video-perception services under staged quality/latency contracts.
fields.example: Teaching example: diversifying retrieved source files fits HoMe; researching and requesting OCR expands MORSE's tool boundary.

fields.question: Why rebuild when construction equivalence is unknown?
fields.answer: Reuse freezes old construction and can hide changed write behavior. The host must review construction paths and validate fingerprints/completed snapshots; unknown or incompatible changes rebuild.
fields.example: Teaching example: retrieval-only edits may reuse after host approval, while schema changes evaluated on old snapshots would hide construction defects.

fields.question: Can a failed episode produce only failure memories?
fields.answer: No. Failed episodes can contain useful actions and successful episodes ineffective ones. Both polarities are derived independently from visible behavior, not hidden final scores.
fields.example: Teaching example: resolving a contact ID correctly but omitting an attachment supports a resolution success lesson and a completeness failure lesson.

fields.question: Why not give task one's reflection immediately to task two?
fields.answer: Every task in a paper block shares the previous frozen memory. The whole block is tested before reflection/maintenance; immediate updates change exposure, cold start and the evaluation protocol.
fields.example: Teaching example: with b=5, tasks one through five use M0; M1 becomes available starting at task six.

fields.question: Is bounded DualPM more lossless than GrepMem?
fields.answer: They target different things. GrepMem retains raw trajectories for grep; DualPM abstracts transferable procedural lessons and may discard detail. Bounded memory guarantees neither detail recovery nor lesson utility.
fields.example: Teaching example: an order number may remain in GrepMem's log while DualPM retains only the procedure to resolve an order ID before acting.

fields.question: Does valid call-local lineage establish a truthful memory?
fields.answer: No. It establishes existing same-polarity references and capacity compliance, not valid generalization. Lineage is model-claimed; controlled callbacks prove L0 plumbing, not LLM reflection.
fields.example: Teaching example: D0 can exist while the lesson wrongly generalizes one success into a rule to skip all future verification.

fields.question: Why does the memory agent not correct from generated video?
fields.answer: The main protocol is open-loop, reading revealed prompts to avoid feeding generation errors back into memory; played shots cannot be rolled back. Reading video is a different ablation.
fields.example: Teaching example: a wrongly rendered coat color should not replace the entity state specified by the revealed prompt.

fields.question: Does hindsight reward reveal the next shot to the planner?
fields.answer: Not under the paper's separation. The policy sees its entity bank, four recent prompts and slot budget; future scripts belong only to reward scoring. Oracle-next-prompt is an upper bound that breaks online constraints.
fields.example: Teaching example: a scorer may later reward an umbrella useful in shot nine, but the shot-eight policy cannot read prompt nine.

fields.question: Do Agentic LongLive and PixVid modify the same layer?
fields.answer: No. The former freezes a generator and injects memory KV at boundaries; PixVid transfers latent DiT knowledge to pixels with a detailer. External consistency memory is not VAE removal.
fields.example: Teaching example: a frozen latent generator can accept entity memory, while a pixel DiT still needs a separate long-horizon memory design.

fields.question: Why does roughly 1% extra generation time not imply cheap single-GPU reproduction?
fields.answer: Agent and prefill work run on extra GPUs, hiding critical-path latency rather than total compute. Six-H100/eight-B200 layouts plus 35B/4B/8B services and full training/evaluation exceed one A100/A30.
fields.example: Teaching example: three extra GPUs working for fifteen seconds during a sixteen-second shot barely change wall time but add substantial GPU-seconds and downloads.
